accused_victim_relationship: Relative (mother-in-law and sister-in-law of the deceased, who were the victim's in-laws)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.498A; IPC s.306 read with s.114 (convicted by trial court and High Court); IPC s.304B read with s.114 and Dowry Prohibition Act s.4 (charged; acquitted by trial court)
evidence_type: Testimonial evidence of relatives, social worker and neighbours; circumstantial evidence; dying declaration; medical evidence from examining doctor
aggravating_circumstances: Repeated cruelty and harassment; victim repeatedly driven out of matrimonial home; repeated beatings; maintenance not paid; victim forced to sleep at odd places
mitigating_circumstances: Accused were present and took victim to hospital when critical; dying declaration said poison was taken by mistake; appellant ages and a child to care for
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.498A (3 years RI and Rs.5,000 fine) and s.306 r/w s.114 (10 years RI and Rs.12,000 fine each); acquitted of s.304B r/w s.114 and DPA s.4
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld
neutral_facts: The victim lived in a joint family with a spouse and in-laws after marriage and had a young daughter. Within about two years of marriage, the victim was allegedly tortured by the spouse and in-laws over demands for dowry and for work performance, and was driven out of the matrimonial home. The victim repeatedly left and stayed at shelters and other places, and was returned to the matrimonial home after mediation by relatives. The victim reported demands for Rs.20,000 and filed a maintenance claim, which went unpaid, and lodged a criminal complaint alleging cruelty and dowry harassment. Several witnesses, including the victim's paternal uncle, that uncle's wife, the victim's brother, a social worker and neighbours, testified that the victim was regularly taunted and physically harassed, that the victim was seen sleeping at odd places, and that heated quarrels took place. One witness said the victim came to him for help, claiming the in-laws were trying to kill her, and had burn marks on her hands. On the day of the incident, the victim ran out of the house calling for help, and one in-law described the condition as epileptic fits. The victim was later found to have consumed poisonous tablets. The accused were in the house at the time and took the victim to hospital when the condition became critical. In a dying declaration, the victim stated the tablets were taken by mistake, and the examining doctor recorded that the victim was stable and conscious enough to give a statement. The victim died. A relative lodged a complaint with the police, after which the scene was examined in a panchanama, witness statements were recorded and the accused were arrested.
offence_severity: Imprisonment up to three years and fine (IPC s.498A); no minimum stated
physical_harm: Death of the victim after consuming poisonous tablets; earlier beatings and burn marks branded on her hands
number_of_offences: 4 charged (IPC s.498A; IPC s.306 r/w s.114; IPC s.304B r/w s.114; Dowry Prohibition Act s.4); 1 finally upheld (s.498A)
financial_property_loss: Alleged dowry demand of Rs.20,000; maintenance of Rs.1,000 per month fixed but not paid
motive: Cruelty and dowry-related harassment by in-laws, accepted as proved by the Court; the Court did not find that this cruelty led to suicide or abetment
key_evidence_accepted: Depositions of PW-6, PW-7, PW-9 and PW-19 on the victim's repeated refuge and harassment; neighbours' testimony (PW-8, PW-10); PW-12's account of the victim seeking help with burn marks; the mother-in-law's 'epileptic fits' remark; the dying declaration and the doctor's evidence on the victim's fitness to make it
witness_credibility: Relatives and neighbours treated as natural witnesses in a matrimonial dispute; objection that they were interested witnesses rejected; no material shown to make their depositions unreliable
post_offence_conduct: Accused took the victim to hospital and the son was called once the mother-in-law realized the gravity of the situation; the Court treated this as showing no abetment
custody_duration: Not stated (appellants surrendered and were undergoing sentence; duration not stated)
bail_history: Not stated (appellants sought enlargement on bail; no bail order described)
trial_duration: offence: 12.11.2006; trial judgment: 21.11.2009; High Court: 23.02.2015; Supreme Court: 14.09.2015
legal_representation: Appellants: Santosh Krishnan, Nikhil Goel, Naveen Goel, Marsook Bafaki. State: Hemantika Wahi, Jesal Wahi, Puja Singh
investigation_status: Complaint registered (I.C.R. No.172 of 2006) at Kodinar Police Station; investigation, panchanama, witness statements and arrests carried out; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.498A and s.306 r/w s.114, acquitted under s.304B and DPA s.4. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence upheld. Supreme Court: s.498A conviction upheld, s.306 conviction set aside, sentence reduced to period undergone
prosecution_argument: Ingredients of ss.498A, 306 and 304B IPC established; victim was harassed and driven out repeatedly; s.113A presumption of abetment proved; concurrent findings of fact should not be disturbed
defence_argument: No independent witnesses; only relatives testified; guilt not proved beyond reasonable doubt; s.113A abetment presumption not proved; dying declaration and doctor's evidence not properly considered
legal_principle_applied: Cruelty under s.498A (Explanation to s.498A) is proved on the evidence; abetment of suicide under s.306 requires proof beyond reasonable doubt, and ss.498A and 306 are independent offences; relatives can be natural witnesses in matrimonial disputes
precedent_relied_upon: Vishwanath Agrawal v. Sarla Vishwanath Agrawal (2012) 7 SCC 288; Bhola Turha v. State of Bihar (1998) 9 SCC 15; Ramesh Kumar v. State of Chhattisgarh (2001) 9 SCC 618
sentencing_rationale: Age of the appellants (mother-in-law around 60; sister-in-law over 35) and the sister-in-law's child to care for; sentence limited to period already undergone
judicial_mitigating_factors: Age of the appellants (around 60 and over 35) and the sister-in-law having a child to take care of
other_sentence_order: Direction to Jail Superintendent, Rajkot Central Prison, to release the appellants forthwith if not required in any other criminal case
